findings.title: Recovery-code creation reads the wrong credential input field
findings.body: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the UserCredentialModel as new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson), which stores the JSON in getValue() and leaves getChallengeResponse() null. This update path reads input.getChallengeResponse() as the credential data, so the federated recovery-code credential is persisted with null credentialData. A later getCredentials() call cannot reconstruct a usable RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from that data, so the new test will fail when rendering or validating the recovery-code form. Read the value from the UserCredentialModel (or populate challengeResponse in the helper consistently).

findings.title: All-codes-used removal does not remove federated credentials
findings.body: After this change getCredential() can return a credential supplied by user storage. When such a credential reports all codes used, this branch calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only removes credentials from Keycloak's local credential store; it does not remove a federated credential from user storage. The exhausted recovery credential therefore remains visible to isConfiguredFor()/getCredential(), and the recovery-code form can still be selected for a credential that has no usable codes (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean may even call get() on an empty next-code Optional). Removal/disablement needs to go through the federated-aware credential-updater API (for example disableCredentialType) or be delegated explicitly to the user-storage provider.

findings.title: Rebuilt federated recovery credential loses the stored credential id
findings.body: getCredentials() rebuilds the recovery-code credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) but never copies myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(). The reconstructed object therefore has a different (newly generated or null) id than the credential originally stored by updateCredential(). Any caller that identifies the credential by id—account REST deletion or the all-codes-used removal in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator—cannot address the stored credential. Set the id on the reconstructed model from myUser.recoveryCodes.
